arxiv-2012-00498.title: Minimal bandwidth for ℂ ∗ {\mathbb{C}}^{*} -actions on generalized Grassmannians Thanks: Supported by the PhD school of the Department of Mathematics of University of Trento
arxiv-2012-00498.creator: Alberto Franceschini
arxiv-2012-00498.description: Abstract . The bandwidth of a ℂ ∗ {\mathbb{C}}^{*} -action of a polarized pair ( X , L ) (X,L) is a natural measure of its complexity. In this paper, we study ℂ ∗ {\mathbb{C}}^{*} -actions on rational homogeneous spaces, determining which provide minimal bandwidth.

arxiv-2012-08029.title: Observations of Energized Electrons in the Martian Magnetosheath
arxiv-2012-08029.description: Abstract This observational study demonstrates that the magnitude and location of energization of electrons in the Martian magnetosheath is more complex than previous studies suggest. Electrons in Mars’s magnetosheath originate in the solar wind and are accelerated by an electric field when they cross the bow shock.

arxiv-2107-05854.title: Exploring the change of semiconductor hole mass under Coulomb scattering
arxiv-2107-05854.creator: Shiue-Yuan Shiau, Monique Combescot
arxiv-2107-05854.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Shiue-Yuan Shiau, Monique Combescot. Semiconductor valence holes are known to have heavy and light effective masses; but the consequence of this mass difference on Coulomb scatterings has been considered intractable and thus ignored up to now. The reason is that the heavy/light index is quantized along the hole momentum that changes in a Coulomb scattering; so, a heavy hole can turn light, depending on the scattering angle.

arxiv-2111-15649.title: Kinematic Hopf Algebra for BCJ Numerators in Heavy-Mass Effective Field Theory and Yang–Mills Theory Preprint: NORDITA 2021-091, QMUL-PH-21-45, SAGEX-21-34, UUITP-60/21
arxiv-2111-15649.creator: Andreas Brandhuber 1, Gang Chen 1, Henrik Johansson 2,3, Gabriele Travaglini 1, Congkao Wen 1
arxiv-2111-15649.description: Abstract We present a closed formula for all Bern-Carrasco-Johansson (BCJ) numerators describing D D -dimensional tree-level scattering amplitudes in a heavy-mass effective field theory with two massive particles and an arbitrary number of gluons. The corresponding gravitational amplitudes obtained via the double copy directly enter the computation of black-hole scattering and gravitational-wave emission.

arxiv-2112-08873.title: Non-equilibrium time-relaxation kinetic model for compressible turbulence modeling
arxiv-2112-08873.creator: Guiyu Cao 1,2, Liang Pan 3, Kun Xu 2,4, Minping Wan 5,6, Shiyi Chen 1,5,6
arxiv-2112-08873.description: Abstract For the first time, the non-equilibrium time-relaxation kinetic model (NTRKM) is proposed for compressible turbulence modeling on unresolved grids. Within the non-equilibrium time-relaxation framework, NTRKM is extended in the form of modified Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook model. Based on the first-order Chapman-Enskog expansion, NTRKM connects with the six-variable macroscopic governing equations.

arxiv-2206-10740.title: Hamiltonian loops on the symplectic blow up along a submanifold Thanks: The author was supported by CONACYT-CB-2017-2018-A1-S-8830 grant
arxiv-2206-10740.creator: Andrés Pedroza
arxiv-2206-10740.description: Abstract . We prove that the fundamental group of the group of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms of the symplectic manifold that is obtain by blowing up a submanifold contains an element of infinite order. We prove this using Weinstein’s morphism and by constructing explicitly such loop of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms. 1991 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary: 57S05 Secondary: 53D35. 1.

arxiv-2311-16318.title: Many-body theory calculations of positronic-bonded molecular dianions
arxiv-2311-16318.creator: J. P. Cassidy, J. Hofierka, B. Cunningham, D. G. Green
arxiv-2311-16318.description: Abstract The energetic stability of positron di-anion systems [A − ; e + ; {}^{-};e^{+}; A - ] is studied via many-body theory, where A − A^{-} includes H - , F - , Cl - and the molecular anions (CN) - and (NCO) - .

arxiv-2403-05536.title: Long-range competition on the torus
arxiv-2403-05536.creator: Bas Lodewijks and Neeladri Maitra
arxiv-2403-05536.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Bas Lodewijks and Neeladri Maitra. We study a competition between two growth models with long-range correlations on the torus 𝕋 n d \mathbb{T}_{n}^{d} of size n n in dimension d d . We append the edge set of the torus 𝕋 n d \mathbb{T}_{n}^{d} by including all non-nearest-neighbour edges, and from two source vertices, two first-passage percolation (FPP) processes start flowing on 𝕋 n d \mathbb{T}_{n}^{d} and compete to cover the sites, where the cost of traversing an edge depends on the torus distance

arxiv-2408-08631.title: Persona is a Double-edged Sword: Mitigating the Negative Impact of Role-playing Prompts in Zero-shot Reasoning Tasks
arxiv-2408-08631.creator: Junseok Kim, Nakyeong Yang, Kyomin Jung
arxiv-2408-08631.description: Abstract Recent studies demonstrate that prompting a role-playing persona to an LLM improves reasoning capability. However, assigning an adequate persona is difficult since LLMs are extremely sensitive to assigned prompts; thus, inaccurately defined personas sometimes hinder LLMs and degrade their reasoning capabilities. In this paper, we first investigate the potential negative impact of injecting persona into language models.

arxiv-2408-11325.title: Telepathic Datacenters: Fast RPCs using Shared CXL Memory Thanks: *These authors contributed equally to this work.
arxiv-2408-11325.creator: Suyash Mahar *, Ehsan Hajyjasini *, Seungjin Lee, Zifeng Zhang, Mingyao Shen, Steven Swanson
arxiv-2408-11325.description: Abstract . Datacenter applications often rely on remote procedure calls (RPCs) for fast, efficient, and secure communication. However, RPCs are slow, inefficient, and hard to use as they require expensive serialization and compression to communicate over a packetized serial network link. Compute Express Link 3.

arxiv-2412-16358.title: Texture- and Shape-based Adversarial Attacks for Vehicle Detection in Synthetic Overhead Imagery
arxiv-2412-16358.creator: Mikael Yeghiazaryan Sai Abhishek Siddhartha Namburu Emily Kim Stanislav Panev, [0.5em] Celso de Melo Brent Lance Fernando De la Torre Jessica K. Hodgins
arxiv-2412-16358.description: Abstract Detecting vehicles in aerial images can be very challenging due to complex backgrounds, small resolution, shadows, and occlusions. Despite the effectiveness of SOTA detectors such as YOLO, they remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks (AAs), compromising their reliability. Traditional AA strategies often overlook the practical constraints of physical implementation, focusing solely on attack performance.

arxiv-2509-05845.title: Golden Ratio Growth and Phase Transitions in Chromatic Counts of Circular Chord Graphs
arxiv-2509-05845.creator: Rogelio N. Lopez-Bonilla, Julian Allagan, Shawn M. Langley, Angel J. Clinton
arxiv-2509-05845.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Rogelio N. Lopez-Bonilla, Julian Allagan, Shawn M. Langley, Angel J. Clinton. We study generalized circular chord graphs 𝒞 n ( k ) \mathcal{C}^{(k)}_{n} , formed from a cycle C n C_{n} by adding fixed-offset chords of length k k and, for even n n , diameters.

arxiv-2511-20308.title: Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney Test of No Group Discrimination
arxiv-2511-20308.creator: M. Grendár
arxiv-2511-20308.description: Abstract . The traditional WMW null hypothesis H 0 : F = G \mathrm{H_{0}}\textrm{:}\,\mathrm{F=G} is erroneously too broad. WMW actually tests narrower H 0 : AUC = 0.5 \mathrm{H_{0}}\textrm{:}\,\textrm{AUC}=0.5 . Asymptotic distribution of the standardized U U statistic (i.e., the empirical AUC) under the correct H 0 \mathrm{H_{0}} is derived along with finite sample bias corrections.

arxiv-2601-14048.title: A systematic study of lepton flavor violating dark matter interactions via indirect detection in effective field theories
arxiv-2601-14048.creator: Sahabub Jahedi, Jin-Han Liang, Yi Liao, Xiao-Dong Ma, Yoshiki Uchida
arxiv-2601-14048.description: Abstract Lepton flavor violating (LFV) interactions involving dark matter (DM) particles remain a largely unexplored area. In this study, we systematically investigate LFV DM interactions within the framework of effective field theories by analyzing astrophysical photons and positrons produced from DM annihilation.

pmc-12369189.title: The prevalence and risk factors of hyperuricemia in patients with Newly-diagnosed coronary artery disease from 2017 to 2021
pmc-12369189.creator: Shaofang Xian, Weiyu Qiu, Shanshan Liu, Shaorong Wu, Jiali Chen
pmc-12369189.description: BackgroundsThis study aimed to evaluate the prevalence and determinants of hyperuricemia in patients with newly-diagnosed coronary artery disease (CAD) after percutaneous coronary intervention.MethodsHyperuricemia was defined as a serum urate level of > 5.6 mg/dl. Medical records and face-to-face interviews were used to collect the demographic characteristics, medical history, lifestyle, self-management, physical examination, and laboratory examination information for each patient.

pmc-12518583.title: Role of anthropogenic mineral circularity in addressing dual challenges of resource supply and waste management in global photovoltaic development
pmc-12518583.creator: Xuehong Yuan, Qingming Song, Ya Liu, Mingxing Huang, Yuting Wang, Zhenming Xu
pmc-12518583.description: Anthropogenic mineral circularity offers a synergistic solution to dual challenges of resource supply and waste management in photovoltaic development. However, the global supply potential of secondary materials remains underexplored, limiting future informed decision-making. Here, we present the global analysis of secondary material supply potential in five photovoltaic technologies under different energy scenarios, using the tailored modeling framework.

pmc-12557771.title: Association between coronary artery calcium and the progression of calcific aortic valve disease: a hospital population-based observational retrospective cohort study
pmc-12557771.creator: Hun-Tae Kim, Jeong Hun Seo, Jun Ho Bae, Tae Jin Kim, You Min Kim, Hyunsu Jo, Sang Hoon Lee, Hang Jae Chung, Dong Sun Han
pmc-12557771.description: AbstractObjectivesTo explore the association between the degree of coronary artery calcium (CAC) and the progression of calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD).DesignA single-centre retrospective cohort study using a hospital-based database.ParticipantsA total of 2898 patients who underwent coronary CT angiography and serial echocardiograms at ≥6 months apart were included. Initial echocardiography was performed within 6 months from the time of CCTA.

pmc-12629850.title: Gender Differences in Quality of Life and Psycho‐Oncological Needs During the First Year After Melanoma Diagnosis
pmc-12629850.creator: Susanne Dugas‐Breit, Jessica Hassel, Martin Dugas, Hans‐Joachim Schulze
pmc-12629850.description: ObjectiveThis study investigated the course of general well‐being and health‐related quality of life (HRQoL) in working‐age melanoma patients during the first year following diagnosis. It also examines the use of psycho‐oncological counseling and rehabilitation, and their impact on QoL.MethodsPatients aged 18–65 years with stage 0 to IIIC melanoma were eligible for this single‐center, prospective cohort study.

pmc-12658519.title: Functional Outcomes, Lung health and Livelihood Outcomes among people With Tuberculosis (FOLLOW-TB): study protocol for a multicentre, prospective cohort study in Canada
pmc-12658519.creator: Jonathon R. Campbell, Allita Rodrigues, Eri Flores, Kamila Romanowski, Tenzin Kunor, Zolelwa Sifumba, Dick Menzies, Kevin Schwartzman, Zofia Zysman-Colman, Andrea Benedetti, James C. Johnston
pmc-12658519.description: IntroductionTuberculosis (TB) is a major global cause of morbidity and mortality. Emerging evidence in high-burden settings suggests significant long-term sequelae among people surviving TB; however, evidence from high-income, low-TB burden settings like Canada is lacking. In a person with TB infection, provision of TB preventive treatment (TPT) can prevent TB disease and its sequelae, but remains underused.

pmc-12811693.title: Severe, Unremitting Piriformis Syndrome Following Yoga and Pilates: A Case Report
pmc-12811693.creator: Abdullatif S Ibrahim, Sameera Hajijama, Nezar Albar, Fatima B Athar, Hamza A Shikh
pmc-12811693.description: Piriformis syndrome (PS) is caused by entrapment of the sciatic nerve due to spasm of the piriformis muscle, resulting in debilitating pain and discomfort. It is challenging to diagnose clinically, particularly when influenced by unusual triggers such as yoga or Pilates.

pmc-13106736.title: Intraoperative fluorescence-guided fresh frozen sectioning for margin control in head and neck cancer: phase 2 clinical trial
pmc-13106736.creator: Thomas S Nijboer, Bas Keizers, Koos Boeve, Daan Roos, Sebastiaan A H J de Visscher, Gyorgy B Halmos, Boudewijn E C Plaat, Henrik K Huizinga, Hendrikus H Boersma, Jan J Doff, Kees-Pieter Schepman, Bert van der Vegt, Max J H Witjes, Floris J Voskuil
pmc-13106736.description: Tumour-free margins ( >5 mm) in head and neck malignancies improve prognosis, possibly impacting the need for adjuvant treatment. In this phase II prospective, non-randomised trial (NCT05499065), we investigate the use of fluorescence imaging using the tumour targeting fluorescent tracer cetuximab-IRDye800CW combined with fresh frozen sectioning to identify inadequate margins intraoperatively in patients with oral squamous cell carcinoma.

pmc-13130676.title: Rubber seed cake supplementation alters meat quality, intestinal health, and gut microbiota in Hu sheep
pmc-13130676.creator: Huwei Zhao, Jinling Hua, Wenwen Lu, Xiaokang Lv, Chao Chen, Yan Liang
pmc-13130676.description: This study aimed to investigate the effects of rubber seed cake (RSC) supplementation on slaughter performance, intestinal health, and gut microbiota in Hu sheep. Forty-eight Hu sheep (17.01 ± 0.57 kg; 3 months old) were randomly allocated to four dietary treatments: 0% (CON), 6% (R6), 12% (R12), and 18% (R18) RSC.

pmc-13387997.title: [18F]Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography ([ 18F]FDG PET) Characterizes Neurodegeneration Levels Across the α‐Synucleinopathy Continuum
pmc-13387997.creator: Beatrice Orso, Ignacio Roura, Pietro Mattioli, Francesco Famà, Federico Massa, Luigi Lorenzini, Andrea Brugnolo, Nicola Girtler, Mattia Losa, Stefano Raffa, Luca Sofia, Monica Roascio, Gabriele Arnulfo, Silvia Morbelli, Matteo Pardini, Dario Arnaldi
pmc-13387997.description: Background[18F]Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography ([18F]FDG PET) represents an endorsed neurodegeneration biomarker in neuronal α‐synucleinopathies. Idiopathic/isolated rapid eye movement (REM) sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) represents a prodromal stage of such disorders.ObjectivesTo assess [18F]FDG PET as a neurodegeneration biomarker, using published brain metabolic disease‐related patterns, and a regional‐based approach, across the prodromal to overt α‐synucleinopathy continuum.

pmc-13530081.title: Integrative pan-cancer analysis of transferrin reveals context-dependent prognostic associations and links to immune and metabolic disease-related programs
pmc-13530081.creator: Weiyi Kong, Ranran Zhang, Zhenyang Fu, Sicheng Chen, Yining Dai, Haomin Xie, Zongrong Lin, Hongcheng Chen, He Li, Yu Chen
pmc-13530081.description: BackgroundIron metabolism is closely linked to tumor biology, yet the pan-cancer significance of transferrin (TF), the major circulating iron-transport protein, remains insufficiently defined. Although TF has been implicated in cancer-related processes, its prognostic relevance, immune associations, and broader disease-related transcriptional context have not been systematically characterized across tumor types.

pmc-13606636.title: Unveiling Disulfidptosis and Cuproptosis Vulnerabilities in Pterygium: A Transcriptomic Analysis and In-Silico Drug Repurposing Strategy
pmc-13606636.creator: İdris Sarıkaya, Recep Kılıç
pmc-13606636.description: Objectives: Pterygium is an invasive, hyperproliferative fibrovascular disorder of the ocular surface characterized by frequent postoperative recurrence and resistance to apoptosis. This study investigated transcriptional alterations in genes related to the regulated cell death pathways disulfidptosis and cuproptosis in pterygium and explored potential pharmacological candidates through in-silico drug repurposing.

pmc-13619508.title: Preoperative CT-derived liver fat fraction and visceral adipose tissue index enhance postoperative recurrence risk stratification in colorectal cancer
pmc-13619508.creator: Ke Yin, Mei Wei, Wenjuan Ba, Rongyu Zhou, Bo Xiao
pmc-13619508.description: BackgroundPostoperative recurrence remains a major cause of treatment failure in colorectal cancer (CRC). We evaluated whether preoperative computed tomography (CT)-derived liver fat fraction (LFF) and visceral adipose tissue index (VATI) improve postoperative recurrence-risk prediction.MethodsThis multi-cohort study included 525 patients after curative-intent surgery: a training cohort (n=260), external validation cohort (n=208), and exploratory prospective cohort (n=57).

uslaw-usc-t10-s8749.title: 10 U.S.C. § 8749 — Civil service mariners of Military Sealift Command: release of drug and alcohol test results to Coast Guard
uslaw-usc-t10-s8749.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t10-s8749.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part IV (General Administration); Chapter 871 (Civilian Employees). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Release of Drug or Alcohol Test Results to Coast Guard.— The Secretary of the Navy may release to the Commandant of the Coast Guard the results of a drug or alcohol test of any employee of the Department of the Navy.

uslaw-usc-t16-s1054.title: 16 U.S.C. § 1054 — Advisory Board; establishment; meetings; functions; quorum; executive secretary
uslaw-usc-t16-s1054.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t16-s1054.description: United States Code, Title 16 (Conservation); Chapter 20 (National Fisheries Center And Aquarium). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. There is established a nonpartisan Advisory Board to be known as the National Fisheries Center and Aquarium Advisory Board. The Advisory Board shall meet from time to time on the call of the Chairman. The functions of the Board shall be to render advice.
